informal_statement: K4 is a strictly weaker logic than S4 in the context of natural numbers, meaning that every theorem provable in K4 is also provable in S4, but there are theorems in S4 that are not in K4.
informal_proof:
To establish that K4 is strictly weaker than S4, we first observe that all the frames validating K4 also validate S4. Specifically, K4 is defined over transitive frames, and since S4 includes transitivity along with additional properties, every theorem of K4 is indeed a theorem of S4.

To demonstrate strictness, we provide a specific formula that is provable in S4 but not in K4. Consider the formula \(\Box(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (\Box A \rightarrow \Box B)\), which is valid in S4 but not necessarily in K4. This illustrates that S4 can derive more complex relationships than K4.

Furthermore, considering the frame conditions, while K4 enforces transitivity, S4 additionally enforces the Church-Rosser condition, which allows for a broader range of valid formulas. This additional constraint in S4 ensures that it is strictly stronger than K4.

Thus, K4 is a subset of S4, and since there exists a formula provable in S4 that is not in K4, we conclude that K4 is strictly weaker than S4.
